name: CacheManager
note: Documentation of what this plugin leaves on a site, for whoever writes a scanner rule or a Hawkeye mute. It is not a trust anchor: nothing should be exempted because this file says so. Verify the plugin directory against the release's checksums.sha256 first.

files.changes_on: self-update from this repository's GitHub releases

cron_events.why: runs the next step of a background clear: after a mode's pause, after a warm-up hands back a cursor, or after a fatal ended the request mid-step

the auto-clear: about 60 seconds after a post matching a rule is published, or, when WP-Cron is more than 2 minutes behind, timestamped just before its oldest due event so it runs first; clears the URLs every waiting rule names, as one per-URL job. Scheduled only when a rule exists and is switched on

since 0.5.0, the next batch of a listings scan somebody started on the Freshness tab: up to 20 Elementor documents within 8 seconds, then the next event, until done. Scheduled only by a press; reads, never writes content

since 0.6.0, only on a site with NitroPack: the oldest-copies scan, every 6 hours, first put on the schedule when a CacheManager screen opens. Each run reads up to 1,000 of NitroPack's cache folders within 2 seconds (file times only), then hashes this site's URLs in batches of 500 to name the kept ones, then the next event. Reads only

options.name: advcm_jobs
options.why: the last 20 clears people started (automatic ones are in advcm_jobs_auto since 0.4.0)

options.name: advcm_jobs_auto
options.why: since 0.4.0, the last 20 automatic clears (auto-clear rules and each post's own page), kept apart so they never push out a clear somebody pressed. A running job is never evicted

options.name: advcm_layers
options.why: per layer, when it was last cleared and how

options.name: advcm_lock_<job id>
options.why: one row while a job is running; deleted when it stops

options.name: advcm_last_error
options.why: the last fault the plugin's guards caught, shown on its screen for a day

options.name: advcm_site_wide_at
options.why: when a whole-site clear last started, for the two-minute gap between them

options.name: advcm_rules
options.why: auto-clear rules: a post type, optionally a term, and up to 10 of this site's own URLs to clear when such a post is published; and the reserved rule own-page, the setting that also clears each saved post's own URL. Written through the rules and settings forms by users holding advcm_purge_hard (editors and administrators since 0.4.0)

options.name: advcm_auto_<rule id>
options.why: one row while a rule is waiting for its clear, with the first 10 posts that triggered it and a count of the rest (for own-page, also up to 40 of their own URLs); deleted when the clear picks it up

options.name: advcm_rules_last
options.why: per auto-clear rule, when it last fired, how many posts triggered it and the job's id and state. Written by the clear, never by the rules form; a rule's entry goes when the rule is deleted

options.name: advcm_settings
options.why: since 0.4.0, the Settings tab: whether own-page ignores saves that change nothing, the post types auto-clear leaves out, the NitroPack choice a new rule starts with, whether a clear of some pages measures their cache age first (since 0.5.0), the longest a page should stay cached for the Freshness tab (since 0.5.1), and the plugin version last seen (for the change log). Read in a post save only after a rule is on, the save is visible and auto-clear is not paused

options.name: advcm_log
options.why: since 0.4.0, who changed what: per tab section, the last 20 changes a person made (time, user id and display name — since 0.5.1, no longer the login — action, one-line summary, value before and after, each cut to 200 characters). Written only by requests a person made, never by WP-Cron

options.name: advcm_freshness
options.why: since 0.5.0, how old each page's cached copy was when a clear somebody started cleared it: the last 100 pages (time, URL cut to 2048 characters, job id, who, HTTP code, age and each layer's age, NitroPack's state and copy age). Written by the clear itself, before its first stage; at most 10 pages per job, never for a whole-site clear

options.name: advcm_freshness_auto
options.why: since 0.5.0, the same for automatic clears, the last 100 pages, kept apart so auto-clear never pushes out what people cleared

options.name: advcm_freshness_stats
options.why: since 0.5.1, what the measurements add up to: per page (at most 200, the page cleared longest ago dropped first; URL cut to 2048 characters) how many clears by hand and automatic, how many found no age, a copy under 10 minutes or one past the cache target, the oldest and the sums for averages, the rules seen, and since 0.5.2 where a redirect pointed (a path cut to 200 characters) and how many clears by hand found a fresh copy; per day, the last 30, the same counts

options.name: advcm_listings
options.why: since 0.5.0, the last listings scan: who started it, a cursor (a post id) and counters, and at most 300 findings (red, amber and custom-query listings, each string cut; green ones only counted). Replaced by the next scan

options.name: advcm_lock_listings
options.why: since 0.5.0, one row while a listings batch runs, naming the document it is reading so a run that dies is stepped over; deleted when the batch ends

options.name: advcm_optimizer_index
options.why: since 0.6.0, the oldest-copies scan: its cursor and counters, and per NitroPack device at most 100 copies twice (the last finished list and the one being built), each a folder name, its time, invalidated and stale flags and a reference to the post, term or home page it is (never the URL). Worst case under 150 KB

options.name: advcm_lock_optimizer
options.why: since 0.6.0, one row while an oldest-copies batch runs, naming the folder it is reading so a run that dies is stepped over; deleted when the batch ends

options.name: advcm_site_wide_log
options.why: since 0.5.1, the times of the whole-site clears in the last hour, at most 4, for the hourly limit

options.name: advcm_rules_paused
options.why: present while an administrator has paused every auto-clear rule; holds when. Read on a post save only when a rule is switched on

wordpress_own_names_touched.name: update_plugins
wordpress_own_names_touched.why: so the Plugins screen re-reads the update list after a release check, as WordPress does after an update

transients.name: advcm_release
transients.why: the updater's cached answer from GitHub

transients.name: advcm_loopback
transients.why: whether the site can reach its own home page, as WordPress needs for its cron; an hour, ten minutes when it cannot

transients.name: advcm_notice_<user id>
transients.why: a one-minute message after a refused press

transients.name: advcm_rate_site
transients.why: since 0.5.1, per-URL clears everybody started in the last minute (at most 30)

transients.name: advcm_rate_<user id>
transients.why: per-URL clears one person started in the last minute (at most 10)

capabilities.name: advcm_purge_hard
capabilities.granted_to: users holding edit_others_posts since 0.4.0 (manage_options before); a site can narrow it with the advcm_purge_hard_base_capability filter

capability_mechanism: a user_has_cap filter that only adds advcm_* keys; never written to roles or user meta

endpoints.why: since 0.4.0, the Settings tab: saves its settings, pauses or resumes auto-clear, switches each post's own page on or off
add, switch on or off, or delete an auto-clear rule; switch the own-page setting on or off; pause or resume them all

endpoints.auth: logged in (wp_ajax_ only, no nopriv), advcm_purge, nonce
endpoints.why: the status screen moves a due background clear where the site's cron cannot wake
since 0.5.0, starts a listings scan on the Freshness tab; reads only

hooks_on_content.why: marks the auto-clear rules a saved post triggers; returns after one option read when no rule is switched on, and never clears anything in the save request

hooks_on_updates.why: after a plugin update, forgets the cached release answer and, since 0.5.1, puts back an auto-clear or a listings scan whose WP-Cron event the update consumed while the plugin was switched off
this plugin updates itself from its GitHub releases whatever the site's per-plugin auto-update toggle says; a site turns that off with the advcm_auto_update filter

filters_offered.name: advcm_auto_update
filters_offered.why: false stops this plugin installing its own releases

filters_offered.name: advcm_purge_base_capability
filters_offered.why: the capability that grants advcm_purge (default edit_others_posts)

filters_offered.name: advcm_purge_hard_base_capability
filters_offered.why: the capability that grants advcm_purge_hard (default edit_others_posts since 0.4.0)

filters_offered.name: advcm_background_available
filters_offered.why: true turns Balanced and Careful back on where DISABLE_WP_CRON is set and a server cron calls wp-cron.php

filters_offered.name: advcm_modes
filters_offered.why: the pauses and warm-up sizes of each mode; pauses where the order forbids them are refused

filters_offered.name: advcm_adapters
filters_offered.why: the cache layers a clear knows; validated, run in stage order whatever order it returns

filters_offered.name: advcm_auto_excluded_post_types
filters_offered.why: the post types an "any content" auto-clear rule does not fire on. Validated; revision, auto-draft and nav_menu_item stay excluded whatever it returns

job_attribution: a clear started from WP-CLI is recorded as WP-CLI, never as the account the command acted as

outbound_requests.why: update check, at most every 12 hours
the update package, through WordPress's own upgrader
warm-up, WordPress's own spawn_cron(), one HEAD of the home page at most hourly from the status screen to check the site can reach itself, and the cache-age check a person asks for on the screen
